title: Vahli Dikri Yojana Gujarat: Benefits, Eligibility, Apply
meta_description: Vahli Dikri Yojana gives Rs 1,10,000 to first two daughters in Gujarat families with income below Rs 2 lakh. Check instalments, eligibility, and how to apply.
disclaimer: Verify all details from the official Gujarat government portal.

hero.one_liner: Gujarat scheme giving ₹1,10,000 to first two daughters in three instalments: at Class 1 entry, Class 9, and age 18.

what_is_it: Vahli Dikri means 'dear daughter' in Gujarati. The name reflects the scheme's goal: making daughters valued by giving families ₹1,10,000 across three life stages.

Vahli Dikri Yojana is Gujarat's scheme for the first two daughters in a family. The total benefit is ₹1,10,000 paid in three instalments at Class 1 entry (₹4,000), Class 9 entry (₹6,000), and age 18 (₹1,00,000).

The scheme targets families with annual income below ₹2 lakh. The large ₹1 lakh payment at age 18 is designed to prevent child marriage by giving families a financial reason to keep daughters unmarried until adulthood.

how_to_apply.description: Attach birth certificate, Aadhaar, income certificate (below ₹2 lakh), bank passbook, and residence proof.

how_to_apply.description: Approved beneficiaries receive instalments directly in their bank account at each milestone (Class 1, Class 9, Age 18).

extra_sections.title: Vahli Dikri Yojana: Rs 1,10,000 in Three Instalments for Gujarat Daughters
extra_sections.content:
Vahli Dikri Yojana is a financial assistance scheme launched by the Government of Gujarat to support families with daughters and reduce female foeticide, child marriage, and school dropout among girls. The scheme provides Rs 1,10,000 per daughter in three instalments: Rs 4,000 when the girl enters Class 1, Rs 6,000 when she enters Class 9, and Rs 1,00,000 when she turns 18 years of age provided she is unmarried and has passed Class 10.

Eligibility is restricted to the first two daughters in the family, families with annual household income below Rs 2 lakh, and girls born on or after 2 August 2019. Applications are submitted through the Women and Child Development Department of Gujarat via the emahilakalyan.gujarat.gov.in portal or through the local Anganwadi centre.

extra_sections.title: Vahli Dikri Yojana: How to Apply (Online and Offline)
extra_sections.content:
Online: Apply through the Digital Gujarat portal (digitalgujarat.gov.in). In rural areas, visit a VCE (Village Computer Entrepreneur) for help with the online form.

Offline: Get the application form from Anganwadi Centre, Gram Panchayat, CDPO (ICDS) office, or District Women and Child Development Officer office. Submit with documents at the same office.

extra_sections.heading: What Vahli Dikri Yojana Covers and Why the Birth Date Matters
content: Vahli Dikri Yojana was formally launched by the Government of Gujarat with effect from 2 August 2019. Only girls born on or after this date are eligible, and there is no exception to this birth-date condition regardless of family income or birth order.

The name Vahli Dikri translates from Gujarati as 'beloved daughter' or 'dear daughter'. The naming reflects the scheme's intent: to shift social attitudes toward daughters and help economically weaker families view the birth of a daughter as a financial asset rather than a burden.

The income limit of Rs 2,00,000 per year is substantially lower than the ceiling for other Gujarat girl-student schemes. Namo Lakshmi and Namo Saraswati Yojana both allow family income up to Rs 6 lakh, while Vahli Dikri targets households that are far more economically constrained.
The scheme covers only the first two daughters in the family. A third or subsequent daughter does not qualify regardless of when she was born or what the family's income is.

steps.title: Class 1 Entry: ₹4,000
steps.desc: First instalment when daughter is admitted to Class 1 in a recognised school.

steps.title: Class 9 Entry: ₹6,000
steps.desc: Second instalment at secondary school admission. School enrollment proof needed.

steps.title: Age 18: ₹1,00,000
steps.desc: Largest instalment. Girl must be unmarried and have passed Class 10.

content: This birth-order restriction is a deliberate policy decision. The scheme aims to shift the mindset of families that are expecting or have had a second daughter, precisely the point where gender-based discrimination in some households peaks.

The birth-order counting refers specifically to daughters, not to all children in the family. A family with a son as the first child and two daughters born afterward has two eligible daughters under this scheme.
The daughters' sequence among all siblings is not what the scheme uses. Only the order of birth among daughters is counted, so the first daughter means the first girl born to the parents.

There is no caste restriction under Vahli Dikri Yojana. Families from SC, ST, OBC, general category, and all other communities are equally eligible as long as the income and birth-date conditions are met.

extra_sections.title: Key point
extra_sections.content: This makes Vahli Dikri a universal low-income entitlement rather than a community-specific benefit.

extra_sections.heading: What Vahli Dikri Yojana Covers and Why the Birth Date Matters (continued)
content: The income certificate must reflect income from all earning members of the household and all sources. Agriculture, wages, salary, self-employment, and rental income all count toward the total.

A family with Rs 1.8 lakh in wages and Rs 40,000 from farming has combined income of Rs 2.2 lakh and does not qualify. The income certificate must list every source, not just the primary earner's salary.

The design of the three-instalment structure is intentional from a child-welfare standpoint. The smaller amounts at Class 1 and Class 9 incentivise enrollment and retention at the two moments when dropout risk is highest.

extra_sections.title: total benefit per daughter across 3 stages
extra_sections.desc: ₹4,000 at Class 1 + ₹6,000 at Class 9 + ₹1,00,000 at age 18 (if unmarried)

content: The Rs 1,00,000 at age 18 arrives precisely when child marriage risk is greatest, giving the family a substantial financial event that is conditional on the daughter remaining unmarried and educated. This timing is the core innovation of the scheme's design.

The bank account registered at application is the one into which all three instalments will be credited over approximately 12 to 13 years. If the account becomes dormant or is closed before the later instalments are due, the family must proactively update the WCD district office with new account details.

Waiting until just before the disbursement date to report an account change often causes delays of several months. Families should review the status of the registered account at each milestone milestone, ideally six months in advance.

A family eligible for Vahli Dikri Yojana is also automatically within the income limit for Namo Lakshmi Yojana, which caps income at Rs 6 lakh. Once the daughter reaches Class 9, the family can enroll her in Namo Lakshmi as well and receive both benefits for the same girl without any conflict.

extra_sections.heading: Vahli Dikri Yojana: Three Instalments Over a Girl's School Life
The Rs 1,00,000 Instalment at Age 18: Conditions and What to Prepare
content: The third instalment of Rs 1,00,000 is the largest component of Vahli Dikri Yojana and the one that requires the most advance preparation. It is released when the girl turns 18, subject to her being unmarried and having passed Class 10.
The rationale for the age-18 condition is directly tied to child marriage prevention. Gujarat law sets 18 as the minimum legal marriage age for girls.

By releasing Rs 1,00,000 at exactly this age, the scheme creates a concrete financial incentive for the family to keep the daughter unmarried through adolescence. The timing makes waiting until legal adulthood the financially advantageous choice for the household.

To receive the Rs 1,00,000, the family must submit proof that the girl has turned 18 and is unmarried. The unmarried status is verified through a self-declaration from the family combined with confirmation from the gram panchayat secretary or urban ward officer.

The district WCD office may also conduct a field visit to cross-verify the information submitted. This verification step is why families are encouraged to initiate the process months before the girl's 18th birthday rather than on the day itself.

extra_sections.title: Key point
extra_sections.content: If the girl marries before turning 18, she permanently loses eligibility for the Rs 1,00,000 instalment.

extra_sections.heading: The Rs 1,00,000 Instalment at Age 18: Conditions and What to Prepare (continued)
content: Families should prepare the age-18 documents well in advance, ideally starting 3 to 6 months before the girl's birthday. The district WCD office requires time to verify the documents and process the disbursement, and late submissions can push the credit into the next processing cycle.

The Rs 1,00,000 is credited to the same bank account registered during the original application. If that account has been closed or changed, the family must update the account details with the WCD district office before the disbursement is initiated.

Requesting an account update very close to the disbursement date can cause significant payment delays. Families should confirm the account is still active and Aadhaar-seeded when the girl is around 17, not just at 18.

Girls enrolled under the scheme since 2019 will reach the Class 9 milestone around 2027 to 2028 and will turn 18 around 2037. Families should retain the original acknowledgment number throughout this period, as it is the reference for all three instalment claims.

Students who are in Class 12 around the time they turn 18 may simultaneously receive Namo Lakshmi benefits and qualify for the Vahli Dikri age-18 payout. Both amounts are credited separately through DBT, so having an active Aadhaar-linked account at that stage handles both disbursements.

extra_sections.content: Vahli Dikri Yojana ties its largest payout of Rs 1,00,000 to a girl reaching age 18 while unmarried and educated, making the scheme a direct financial counter-incentive to child marriage and dropout in Gujarat's low-income families. The three-stage design ensures money arrives at each critical risk point: school entry at Class 1, secondary enrollment at Class 9, and adulthood at 18. Families with daughters born after 2 August 2019 and annual household income below Rs 2 lakh should register through their local Anganwadi centre as early as possible to lock in their eligibility for all three instalments.
extra_sections.text: Vahli Dikri is not charity. It is the government recognising that raising a daughter costs money, and putting that money where it matters: at school entry, at secondary school, and at adulthood.

extra_sections.heading: Common Errors and Overlooked Details in Vahli Dikri Applications
content: One of the most frequent mistakes is submitting an income certificate that does not include all sources of household income. The Rs 2 lakh limit applies to combined income from wages, farming, business, rent, and any other regular source.

A family with Rs 1.6 lakh in wages and Rs 60,000 in agricultural income has total income of Rs 2.2 lakh and does not qualify, even though wage income alone is below the limit. The income certificate must capture every source to be accepted.
The income certificate must also be a recent one. District offices generally require it to have been issued within the current or immediately preceding financial year.

An outdated income certificate will be rejected, and the family must obtain a fresh one before the application can proceed. This requirement applies at each instalment claim milestone, not only at the initial application.

Some families assume the birth-date cutoff of 2 August 2019 refers to the date the birth certificate was registered rather than the actual date of birth. The scheme uses only the actual date of birth as shown on the certificate.

extra_sections.heading: Vahli Dikri Eligibility Quick Check
qualify: First or second daughter in the family
Enrolled in recognised school (for education instalments)
disqualify: Girl married before age 18 (loses final ₹1 lakh)

content: If the date of birth on the certificate is on or after 2 August 2019, the girl qualifies even if the certificate was issued years after the birth. The date of registration on the certificate is irrelevant to eligibility.

Late birth registration is common in some rural districts of Gujarat, and a certificate may show a registration year of 2021 for a child born in 2019. As long as the date of birth on the certificate is on or after 2 August 2019, the WCD office should accept the application.

If the district office raises concerns about late registration, families can supplement the birth certificate with a hospital discharge record or ASHA worker entry that shows the actual birth date. The ICDS sector supervisor can help navigate such documentation disputes.

Gujarat administers several women-focused schemes through emahilakalyan.gujarat.gov.in. When accessing the portal, confirm you are on the Vahli Dikri section and not inadvertently submitting for a different scheme.
The portal lists all schemes by name in both Gujarati and English. Searching specifically for Vahli Dikri on the portal brings up the correct application page directly.

Families in remote or tribal areas who cannot access the online portal should approach the ICDS supervisor for their sector. The ICDS supervisor can submit the application on the family's behalf and track approval status with the district office.

extra_sections.title: Key point
extra_sections.content: Once enrolled, a girl's application remains active across all three instalments under the original acknowledgment number.

extra_sections.heading: Common Errors and Overlooked Details in Vahli Dikri Applications (continued)
content: The family only needs to inform the WCD office that a milestone has been reached and provide the relevant supporting document for that instalment. Keeping the original acknowledgment number safe from the day of application through the girl's 18th birthday is therefore essential.

The Class 10 pass condition for the Rs 1,00,000 instalment means the girl must have completed the Class 10 board examination. A girl who has studied through Class 12 and passed would also satisfy this condition, as she has completed Class 10 as part of her schooling.

A girl who dropped out after Class 8 and never appeared for the Class 10 board examination does not meet the educational condition for the third instalment even if she is otherwise unmarried and has reached 18. The pass condition requires actual completion of the Class 10 examination, not just school enrollment up to that level.

Families sometimes ask whether an adopted daughter qualifies under Vahli Dikri Yojana. The scheme's eligibility framework focuses on the girl being the first or second daughter in the family unit, rather than specifying biological relationship.

Whether an adopted daughter qualifies should be confirmed directly with the district WCD office. The ICDS supervisor can assist with this and will advise on the supporting documentation needed to establish family membership and birth order.

content: Another common question is whether the scheme covers a second daughter if the first daughter has died before the second daughter was born. Whether the surviving daughter is treated as the first or second daughter in the scheme's records is a matter for the district WCD office to determine based on the family's documentation.

For Class 1 enrollment, the school enrollment certificate is the standard document used to confirm the milestone and trigger the first instalment. The school must be a recognised institution under the Gujarat Education Department or a board recognised by the state.

Enrollment in an unrecognised school may not be accepted for milestone verification. Families should check that their chosen school is on the Gujarat Government's list of approved schools before the girl is enrolled, to avoid a complication at the first instalment stage.

When claiming the second instalment at Class 9, the family must provide proof of enrollment from the school. This is typically a school admission receipt or an enrollment confirmation issued by the school principal.

The WCD office or ICDS supervisor will specify the exact document format required for each instalment claim. Asking the supervisor in advance what documents will be needed for the upcoming milestone saves time at the actual claim stage.

faqs.question: What is Vahli Dikri Yojana Gujarat?
faqs.answer:
Vahli Dikri Yojana is a Government of Gujarat scheme that provides Rs 1,10,000 in three instalments to families with daughters to reduce child marriage and dropout. It gives Rs 4,000 when the girl enters Class 1, Rs 6,000 when she enters Class 9, and Rs 1,00,000 when she turns 18 provided she is unmarried and has passed Class 10.

The scheme covers only the first two daughters in families with annual income below Rs 2 lakh, and girls must have been born on or after 2 August 2019.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for Vahli Dikri Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Eligibility requires the girl to be the first or second daughter in the family, born on or after 2 August 2019, and a resident of Gujarat. The family's annual household income from all sources must be below Rs 2,00,000.

There is no caste restriction and families from SC, ST, OBC, and general categories are all eligible. Third or subsequent daughters in the family do not qualify regardless of income.

faqs.question: How much money does Vahli Dikri Yojana give?
faqs.answer:
Vahli Dikri Yojana gives a total of Rs 1,10,000 per eligible daughter across three instalments. The first instalment is Rs 4,000 at Class 1 enrollment, the second is Rs 6,000 at Class 9 enrollment, and the third is Rs 1,00,000 when the girl turns 18 if she is unmarried and has passed Class 10.

Both the first and second daughter in the family can each receive the full Rs 1,10,000.

faqs.question: What is the income limit for Vahli Dikri Yojana?
faqs.answer:
The family must have annual household income below Rs 2,00,000 (Rs 2 lakh) from all sources. Income from salary, wages, agriculture, business, rent, and any other source is counted.

An income certificate issued by a Revenue authority in Gujarat confirming income below Rs 2 lakh is a mandatory document for the application. Certificates that include only one source of income or that are outdated will typically be rejected.

faqs.question: How to apply for Vahli Dikri Yojana online?
faqs.answer:
Yes. You can apply online through the Digital Gujarat portal (digitalgujarat.gov.in).

In rural areas, VCE operators help with the online form. You can also apply offline at the Anganwadi centre or CDPO office.

faqs.question: What happens to the Rs 1,00,000 if the girl gets married before 18?
faqs.answer:
If the girl marries before turning 18, she permanently forfeits eligibility for the Rs 1,00,000 final instalment. The forfeiture is irreversible even if the marriage is later dissolved.

The first and second instalments already received are not recovered by the government, but the Rs 1,00,000 will not be disbursed. The scheme's third instalment is specifically designed as an incentive for delaying marriage until legal adulthood.

faqs.question: Can a girl receive both Vahli Dikri Yojana and Namo Lakshmi Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Yes, both schemes can be received simultaneously once the girl reaches Class 9. Vahli Dikri provides Rs 6,000 at Class 9 enrollment and Rs 1,00,000 at age 18, while Namo Lakshmi provides monthly stipends from Class 9 through Class 12 and board exam bonuses totalling Rs 50,000.

Vahli Dikri requires family income below Rs 2 lakh, while Namo Lakshmi allows income up to Rs 6 lakh, so any family eligible for Vahli Dikri is automatically eligible for Namo Lakshmi as well.

faqs.question: Is Vahli Dikri Yojana available for girls born before 2 August 2019?
faqs.answer:
No. Vahli Dikri Yojana is limited to girls born on or after 2 August 2019, the date the scheme was launched.

Girls born before this date are not eligible regardless of family income, birth order, or any other factor. Families whose daughters do not qualify for Vahli Dikri due to birth date should explore other schemes such as Namo Lakshmi Yojana, which provides support for girls in Class 9 to 12 without a birth-date cutoff.

faqs.question: Can I apply for Vahli Dikri Yojana online?
faqs.answer:
Yes. You can apply online through the Digital Gujarat portal (digitalgujarat.gov.in).

In rural areas, VCE operators help with the online form. You can also apply offline at the Anganwadi centre or CDPO office.

faqs.question: What does Vahli Dikri mean?
faqs.answer: Vahli Dikri means 'dear daughter' in Gujarati. The scheme was named to promote the value of daughters in families.
